axes.name: Strong cross-client primitives
axes.definition: Whether byte-range locks, O_EXCL create, atomic rename, and shared sqlite/git actually work between clients/pods, not just inside one.

axes.name: Read freshness across clients
axes.definition: How stale another client's view of your write can be — from enforced close-to-open down to snapshot-until-explicit-sync.

axes.name: CAS / conditional-write fidelity
axes.definition: What If-Match / If-None-Match actually bind: which writer populations, detection vs refusal, cooperative vs enforced.

axes.name: Acked-write crash durability
axes.definition: Which failure domain an acked write/fsync survives before the write-back tier lands it in S3.

axes.name: Multi-writer arbitration
axes.definition: Who arbitrates concurrent writers to the same tree and what a second writer experiences — serialized, refused, or merely detected.

axes.name: Foreign-write conflict surfacing
axes.definition: The fate of an out-of-band/foreign write against a live tree: silently lost, undetected, or preserved-and-surfaced.

cells.rationale: flint-lite-consistency.html: "opens, byte-range locks, O_EXCL and rename are real across every client of the share"; the comparison doc scores locks/O_EXCL/rename "real across every client", and shared sqlite/git across clients is shipped and cluster-proven (multicluster P0). krb5p identical — RPCSEC_GSS wraps the RPCs, it does not change what they mean.

flint-fuse-consistency.html (designed, deprioritized): "no cross-pod locks, no shared sqlite / git — refused, not discouraged. ENOLCK and EXDEV at the FUSE layer" — but one real primitive survives: "O_EXCL as a synchronous If-None-Match:* PUT — the one strongly consistent cross-pod primitive in this mode."

flint-lean-architecture.html: "PLAIN FILES — a real local filesystem, full POSIX, zero interception" — zero interception means nothing can be made cross-pod, not even FUSE's opt-in O_EXCL; flint-lean-plan.md §3 (built through Phase 3): cross-pod is "snapshots + sync only". sqlite/git work single-pod only (Phase 2 battery).

flint-lite-consistency.html: another node sees your write "at close-to-open — the hub is the one coherence authority"; the fleet guide adds the only staleness residuals (a file held open reads its open()-time snapshot; readdir cached up to acdirmax 60s). Strongest cross-client view in the tree.

flint-fuse-consistency.html (as designed): another pod reads "a consistent snapshot at most one flush interval + one revalidation old; never read-your-peers'-writes" — a bounded, automatic staleness window, with the comparison doc's revalidate-on-open upgrade reaching "close-to-open — NFS parity for single-writer workspaces".

flint-lean-plan.md §3 states v1 does not solve "cross-pod live visibility (snapshots + sync only)" and the sync verb is "harness-invoked... never background" — a reader pod's staleness is unbounded until someone explicitly syncs, weaker than FUSE's automatic flush+revalidate cadence.

flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md: v1.30 file API PUT/DELETE/move carry If-Match — "a competing write answers 412 instead of silently losing your edit" — served against the live view with no RPO lag; but "If-Match is detection between API callers, not exclusion against the mount" and "an ETag changes when a file is evicted or hydrated" (spurious 412s).

flint-fuse-architecture.html (designed): "the store's own CAS — If-Match on every publish... CAS is detection and fencing, not serialization: it binds only writers that cooperate" — publishes are untorn CAS-guarded generations and O_EXCL rides a true If-None-Match:* PUT, but every pod holds prefix write credentials, so the regime stays cooperative.

flint-lean-architecture.html: "the gateway is the enforcement point these cells always lacked — detection becomes refusal"; pods hold zero bucket write credentials, the conformance gate has must-FAIL arms ("a stale If-Match that MUST 412; If-None-Match:* over an existing key that MUST 412"), and Phase-3 gateway verbs ship per-request epoch validation (plan status) — though sidecar barriers still CAS cells directly through the proxy rather than the gateway verbs.

flint-lite-consistency.html: "an acked write is crash-durable on the hub's PVC immediately" — it "survives hub crash, pod reschedule, node crash — anything that leaves the PVC intact"; only PVC loss converts the RPO into loss, and hibernate is verify-then-delete on rpoClean. Not 5 because fsync still does not mean S3.

flint-fuse-consistency.html: fsync ack is "durable to the pod's emptyDir... NOT the pod. NOT S3" and "the loss boundary is POD DEATH... on a spot fleet, pod death is routine — not a disaster scenario"; preStop drains ~9–15 GiB inside a 120s spot notice, a hard crash drains nothing.

flint-lean-plan.md §7 (built): "Loss bounds: RPO per pod; preStop drain best-effort... hard crash drains nothing" — the same emptyDir durability domain as FUSE, plus a stated residual FUSE's interception avoids: "torn whole-file uploads of files written DURING a forced barrier" (§3).

flint-consistency-comparison.html, "two writers, one file": "serialized — locks and share reservations are real" — the hub is the arbiter because "NFS's round-trip through the hub is exactly where opens, locks and renames get ordered"; a second writer blocks or is denied, never corrupts.

flint-consistency-comparison.html: two writers on one file are "out of contract — one writer per subtree, lease-enforced", and the lease is the cooperative CAS that "binds only writers that cooperate" (fuse-architecture); unclean death adds a 60–110s lockout, and a credentialed non-cooperator is only detected, not stopped.

Still one writer per subtree, but the arbitration is enforced rather than cooperative: flint-lean-plan.md §2.2 takeover fence rotation makes "a deposed predecessor's in-flight manifest CAS 412", per-request epoch validation rejects below-cell epochs, and the barrier-window/inbox cell serializes sidecar-vs-HITL writers with a stated starvation bound (built through Phase 3).

flint-lite-consistency.html: "S3-side writes against a live hub are out of contract. three fates: silently destroyed by local-wins, undetected while resident, or adopted as truth by a hydration 412" — and between the two doors, the fleet guide says a REST-vs-mount race is server-ordered but "the ETag will not save you": last-writer-wins, silently.

flint-fuse-consistency.html: "same three fates as hub mode — destroyed, undetected, or adopted; the project role is read-only for a reason" — the same silent-fate matrix, mitigated only structurally (read-only project role, prefix-scoped IRSA narrowing who can write foreign at all).

The one axis lean was rebuilt around (Phase 1+2 shipped): foreign manifest entries "are PRESERVED and queued into the inbox for the next sync — never dropped, never deleted", the 412 policy parks foreign ETags into a machine-readable conflict report ("never If-Match-overwrite an ETag the sidecar did not itself publish"), and the Phase-6 oracle is explicit: "both versions recoverable, conflict surfaced, never a silent winner" (flint-lean-plan.md).

proposal.note: Consistency is arbitration, not proximity to S3 — the comparison doc's own verdict — so the hub (one series for sec=sys and krb5p: RPCSEC_GSS is dormant per pnfs-operator-runbook.md and wraps authentication, not coherence) sweeps every strong axis: primitives, freshness, and arbitration are 5s because every operation takes the round-trip where ordering is manufactured. The inversion is the chart's story: the hub is nearly the weakest at foreign-write conflict surfacing (the "three fates": destroyed, undetected, or adopted), while lean — weakest at live coherence, with snapshots-plus-explicit-sync freshness — posts the strongest CAS and conflict scores because its gateway turns the cooperative CAS regime into refusal and its load-bearing inbox/merge-manifest guarantees "never a silent winner." FUSE sits between on every axis but leads lean nowhere except freshness, and both direct modes share the same 1.5 durability floor: an acked fsync means emptyDir, and emptyDir means pod-lifetime.

verdicts.reason: Quote verified verbatim in docs/flint-lite-consistency.html ('opens, byte-range locks, O_EXCL and rename are real across every client of the share') and docs/flint-consistency-comparison.html ('real across every client of the share'; 'serialized — locks and share reservations are real'). Shipped state backs it: lock-machinery hardening fixes B1/B2 (48de6d1) and B7 (56d...) are at HEAD, and the fleet guide sells sqlite/git/compilers on the mount (line 21) with cross-node/cross-cluster close-to-open (line 552). The only weakening I found — lease expiry can release a partitioned client's locks (fleet guide lines 634-644) — is standard NFS lease semantics present in any 5-worthy implementation, and the co_ownerid notification-delivery hazard has a documented remedy (unique client names) plus the v1.36 fixes. Relative to FUSE 1.5 (ENOLCK, EXDEV — 'refused, not discouraged') and Lean 1, this is the only approach where the primitives exist at all. krb5p wraps the RPCs without changing their meaning, so it inherits the 5.

docs/flint-lite-consistency.html: another node sees the write 'at close-to-open — the hub is the one coherence authority', and the axis definition explicitly tops out at 'enforced close-to-open', which is exactly what this is. The fleet guide even measures it (REST write visible on a live mount 'in under a second', lines 920-926) and its only residuals — a file held open reads its open()-time snapshot, readdir cached up to acdirmax 60s (lines 931-936) — are inherent to close-to-open, not below it. Against FUSE 2.5 ('RPO-stale snapshot — at most one flush interval + one revalidate old') and Lean 1.5 (snapshot-until-sync), 5 is the correct relative anchor; a 4.5 for the acdirmax residual would be a taste quibble the axis definition itself rules out.

Both halves of the rationale check out in docs/flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md: PUT/DELETE/move carry If-Match and 'a competing write answers 412 instead of silently losing your edit' (lines 422-424), dispatched 'in-process through the hub's own dispatcher' so it binds the live view with no RPO lag (436-441); but 'If-Match is detection between API callers, not exclusion against the mount... a REST writer and a mounted writer racing on the same file are ordered by the server but the ETag will not save you' (940-944) and 'an ETag changes when a file is evicted or hydrated' (945-948). The mounted population — the majority writer population here — is outside the CAS regime, which is precisely why Lean sits above at 4 (flint-lean-architecture.html: 'the cooperative CAS regime becomes ENFORCED: non-holders get no URL; If-Match is required' — the proxy binds ALL writers). 3 between FUSE's cooperative opt-in 2.5 and Lean's enforced 4 is right.

docs/flint-lite-consistency.html states it verbatim: 'an acked write is crash-durable on the hub's PVC immediately' and 'survives hub crash, pod reschedule, node crash — anything that leaves the PVC intact', with hibernate as verify-then-delete on rpoClean (lines 142-144). The comparison doc's fsync row gives NFS 'pod and node death — the PVC holds it' vs FUSE 'container crashes only — emptyDir dies with the pod', justifying the 2-point gap over FUSE/Lean at 1.5. The cap below 5 is also doc-grounded: 'a successful NFS write is NOT in S3' and 'there is no fsync-to-S3 verb'; the fsync⇒S3 upgrade is the strict journal, which is designed-only (flint-strict-architecture.html, no build commits in git log). 3.5 is the defensible middle: survives everything except PVC/volume destruction, with a stated RPO to S3.

docs/flint-consistency-comparison.html answers this row directly: 'two writers, one file: serialized — locks and share reservations are real' vs FUSE 'out of contract — one writer per subtree, lease-enforced', and reason 2 ('the extra hop was the serialization point... where opens, locks and renames get ordered') plus the figcaption's concession that 'an arbiter that answers in milliseconds is a server by definition, and flint already ships it — the hub' make the hub the definitional top of this axis. A second writer blocks on a lock or is denied a share reservation — never corrupts — and the arbitration is enforced by the server regardless of sec=sys vs krb5p. Lean's 2.5 (publish-granularity lease arbitration at the gateway, not per-op) and FUSE's 1.5 calibrate correctly below it. No doc evidence against 5.

The quote is verbatim (flint-lite-consistency.html lines 146-148: 'S3-side writes against a live hub are out of contract... silently destroyed by local-wins, undetected while resident, or adopted as truth by a hydration 412') and the dual-door race adds 'the ETag will not save you' (fleet guide 941-943) — all fates silent, so NFS belongs at the bottom band. I specifically tested the FUSE gap, since flint-fuse-consistency.html says 'same three fates as hub mode — destroyed, undetected, or adopted' (lines 150-151): the half-point survives because the hub's local-wins destroy-surface is the whole share (one publisher over the entire tree, plus the two-door last-writer-wins race that FUSE doesn't have), while FUSE scopes destruction to the writer's own subtree and foreign generations of other subtrees arrive as clean manifest-revalidated snapshots. And 1.5 rather than 1 is defensible because two of the three fates preserve rather than lose data (adoption; server-ordered door races are untorn). Lean's 4 anchor is real: the inbox holds HITL/foreign writes 'never dropped, never deleted' (docs/plans/flint-lean-plan.md line 119), enforced at every barrier.

1.5 survives. flint-fuse-consistency.html: 'no cross-pod locks, no shared sqlite / git — refused, not discouraged. ENOLCK and EXDEV', with exactly one real cross-pod primitive ('O_EXCL as a synchronous If-None-Match:* PUT — the one strongly consistent cross-pod primitive in this mode'). The arch doc's death list (fcntl→ENOLCK, cross-subtree rename→EXDEV, shared mmap refused, sqlite/git→hub) confirms the rest are absent-by-refusal. The +0.5 over Lean's 1 is earned: lean is 'PLAIN FILES... zero interception' (flint-lean-architecture.html), so O_EXCL/flock succeed locally with zero cross-pod meaning — the silent-local-success hazard FUSE 'enforces away'; FUSE has one genuine global primitive plus honest errno. Far below NFS's 5 ('locks · O_EXCL · rename — real across every client'). Docs-only, scored as designed — correct.

2.5 survives even discounting the revalidate-on-open upgrade (which sits in the comparison doc's 'upgrades' panel, not the base design). Base design alone: another pod reads 'a consistent snapshot at most one flush interval + one revalidation old; never read-your-peers'-writes' (flint-fuse-consistency.html), with automatic revalidation ('conditional GET of the subtree manifest ETag; sweep only when seq advances' — fuse-architecture). Bounded-automatic ~60-120s staleness sits correctly between NFS's enforced close-to-open (5) and Lean's 1.5, which is snapshot-until-explicit-sync: 'Cross-pod live visibility (snapshots + sync only)' and no online refresh — the sync verb is harness-invoked (flint-lean-plan.md §3, §sync verb). The comparison doc marks this the weaker cell vs hub, which the 2.5-point gap to NFS already prices in.

2.5 puts FUSE strictly below the hub's 3, and the docs refute that ordering on this axis's own criteria. Populations bound: FUSE-mode publishes are 100% CAS-guarded ('If-Match on every publish', 'If-Match / If-None-Match:* · epoch guard checked · manifest CAS' — flint-fuse-architecture.html), and the proposer missed 'bucket policy enforces conditional writes (s3:if-none-match, GA 2024-11): vandalism becomes auditable forgery, not blind clobber' — conditional-write discipline is mandatory for every writer of the bucket. The hub's 3, by contrast, rests on a CAS that its own doc caveats: 'If-Match is detection between API callers, not exclusion against the mount... the ETag will not save you' plus spurious 412s ('An ETag changes when a file is evicted or hydrated... Nothing the user did changed') — flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md — i.e. the hub's dominant writer population (the mount) escapes the ETag entirely, and it too is cooperative. Detection vs refusal: FUSE's 412 is store-atomic refusal; the hub's is detection-grade. So FUSE ties NFS at 3 — not above, because FUSE exposes no app-visible conditional-update verb (only O_EXCL create; the If-Match machinery is internal, binding sidecar generations at flush cadence) and holder arbitration stays cooperative ('CAS is detection and fencing, not serialization: it binds only writers that cooperate') — which is exactly the gap Lean's 4 closes ('non-holders get no URL; If-Match is required', pods hold zero credentials).

1.5 survives. fsync ack is 'durable to the pod's emptyDir — survives app, sidecar, container crashes. NOT the pod. NOT S3.' and 'the loss boundary is POD DEATH... on a spot fleet, pod death is routine — not a disaster scenario' (flint-fuse-consistency.html); the failure matrix adds 'agent NODE crash... drains nothing — loses the unflushed set (hot files: unbounded)' and preStop drains only ~9-15 GiB inside the 120s notice, ~2-3 GiB at the default 30s grace, 'hard crash drains 0' (fuse-architecture p4). Correctly 2 below NFS's 3.5 (ack 'survives hub crash, pod reschedule, node crash — anything that leaves the PVC intact' — lite-consistency) and correctly EQUAL to Lean's 1.5: lean's workspace is the same pod-lifetime emptyDir ('emptyDir — the whole workspace, materialized', preStop final publish barrier — lean-architecture), the identical durability domain. Strict journal mode (fsync⇒S3) is an upgrade panel item in both direct modes and is consistently uncounted in both 1.5s.

1.5 survives. Comparison doc: two writers, one file is 'out of contract — one writer per subtree, lease-enforced' and 'after a crash + restart... a 60-110s lease lockout after unclean death' (measured 80-110s in fuse-architecture p4). I tested the strongest counter-evidence — 'one writer per workspace subtree — enforced by the subtree lease + IAM, not by hope' — but the docs' own verdict keeps the score low: the FUSE arch says 'CAS is detection and fencing, not serialization: it binds only writers that cooperate', and the lean doc explicitly frames its 1-point-higher gateway as the fix for FUSE's regime: 'the gateway is the enforcement point these cells always lacked — detection becomes refusal' / 'a non-holder is refused a URL, not merely detected after the fact' (flint-lean-architecture.html). That doc-stated upgrade IS the FUSE(1.5)→Lean(2.5) gap, and NFS's 5 ('serialized — locks and share reservations are real') stays far above both.

2 survives, narrowly. The refutation case was real: the comparison doc lists 'console PUTs against a live tree: the same three fates' under 'identical in both', and bucket versioning is NOT a FUSE differentiator (hub mode also requires it: 'must already exist, versioning on' — flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md). But the +0.5 over NFS's 1.5 still stands on FUSE-only designed machinery: 'bucket policy enforces conditional writes (s3:if-none-match, GA 2024-11): vandalism becomes auditable forgery, not blind clobber' (fuse-architecture) — an accidental unconditional foreign PUT is refused at the bucket door, and a deliberate one is auditable — plus per-subtree IAM scoping and the read-only project role, none of which the hub's posture documents. The 2-point gap to Lean's 4 is solid: only lean parks and surfaces foreign writes ('foreign entries... surfaced in the inbox for the next sync — never dropped, never deleted', 'both versions recoverable, conflict surfaced, never a silent winner' — flint-lean-plan.md); FUSE keeps the three silent fates.

Score 1 survives. flint-lean-architecture.html: '/workspace PLAIN FILES — a real local filesystem, full POSIX, zero interception' — no interception layer exists to make any POSIX primitive cross-pod, and flint-lean-plan.md §3 confirms cross-pod is 'snapshots + sync only'. Tried to refute downward (lean cannot even refuse like FUSE's ENOLCK — a local flock silently means nothing cross-pod) but the nonzero floor is earned: claim-cell CAS gives cross-pod exclusivity at workspace granularity and single-pod sqlite/git are fully proven (Phase 2 battery, commit 1a45ed9). The half-point below FUSE is correctly ordered: flint-fuse-consistency.html grants FUSE one real cross-pod primitive ('cross-pod O_EXCL create: strongly consistent (sync PUT)') that lean structurally cannot offer.

Score 1.5 survives. flint-lean-plan.md §3: 'Cross-pod live visibility (snapshots + sync only)'; §2.1: the sync verb is 'harness-invoked (exec/localhost HTTP), never background'; §1: 'no online refresh (sync is explicit)'. A reader pod's staleness is unbounded until an explicit sync — strictly weaker than FUSE's bounded 'at most one flush interval + one revalidation old' (flint-fuse-consistency.html). Tried to push to 1, but the writer still publishes at floorSecs cadence, so gateway snapshot/browser reads are exactly as RPO-fresh as FUSE's published view — only the reader-pod pull side degrades, and the 1-point gap below FUSE's 2.5 prices exactly that.

Score 4 survives, including the strongest attack: 'detection becomes refusal' (flint-lean-architecture.html) is partly grade-2 phrasing while grade-1 proxy is the decided posture, and §3 admits 'within-project enforcement is gateway-validated + CAS-cooperative'. But the bound writer population is total — 'pods hold ZERO bucket write credentials' — the conformance gate has must-FAIL arms ('a stale If-Match that MUST 412; If-None-Match:* over an existing key that MUST 412 — stripping is only observable as a forbidden success', plan §2.2), and repo state confirms per-request epoch validation SHIPPED (a602e08, plan status 2026-08-25: 'P5's teeth on every gateway-mediated write' — my memory note that P5 did not exist is stale). Versus NFS's 3 ('detection NOT serialisation, weakest under load', binding only hub-door writers) and FUSE's 2.5 (cooperative, pods hold creds), 4 is right; not 4.5 because sidecar barriers 'currently CAS the cells directly through the proxy' (stated open gap) and the within-project residual is cooperative.

Score 1.5 (tied with FUSE) survives. flint-lean-plan.md §7: 'Loss bounds: RPO per pod; preStop drain best-effort within the §2.1 arithmetic; hard crash drains nothing' — the identical emptyDir failure domain as FUSE ('fsync ack durable to the pod's emptyDir... NOT the pod. NOT S3.', flint-fuse-consistency.html). Tried both directions: lean has capture-fidelity residuals FUSE lacks ('mtime-granularity scan evasion' and 'torn whole-file uploads of files written DURING a forced barrier', §3), while FUSE has ENOTCONN/restart-in-place choreography lean lacks (lean's restart matrix: 'no resurrection, lease self-recognized, dirt rebuilt by rescan', §7). Both are publish-path or recovery-shape differences; the axis's actual failure domain — survives container crash, dies with the pod — is identical, so the tie stands.

Score 2.5 survives. Enforced, not cooperative: plan §2.2 takeover fence rotation ('a deposed predecessor's in-flight manifest CAS 412s'), per-request epoch validation 'rejecting writes whose epoch is below the subtree cell's' (shipped, a602e08), and the barrier-window/inbox cell serializing sidecar-vs-HITL writers with a stated starvation bound ('after N consecutive HITL refusals, the next barrier admission defers to the pending write'). A second writer is refused (zero bucket credentials; HITL 'refuse with Retry-After'), versus FUSE's 'out of contract — one writer per subtree, lease-enforced' detection posture (flint-consistency-comparison.html) — a full point above FUSE is earned, and half of NFS's 5 ('serialized — locks and share reservations are real') is right since lean still admits only one general writer per subtree. The ~60-110s unclean-death lockout with the P4 fencing actor deferred does not drag it below 2.5 because FUSE carries the identical lockout.

Score 4 survives; every quoted mechanism verified in flint-lean-plan.md and shipped in 1a45ed9: foreign manifest entries 'are PRESERVED and queued into the inbox for the next sync — never dropped, never deleted' (§2.1 step 5), the 412 policy 'park the path, emit it in the conflict report, never If-Match-overwrite an ETag the sidecar did not itself publish', etag-guarded GC ('a key whose ETag the sidecar does not recognize is never deleted'), sync's 'machine-readable conflict report + exit status', and the Phase 6 oracle 'both versions recoverable, conflict surfaced, never a silent winner'. Against NFS/FUSE's shared out-of-contract posture ('same three fates as hub mode — destroyed, undetected, or adopted', flint-fuse-consistency.html), lean is categorically strongest — this is the axis the v2 review rebuilt (HITL amputation found independently by three dimensions, §10). 4 rather than higher is correct: surfacing waits for the next barrier/sync, and the Phase 6 drill leg is not yet run.

axes.name: Streaming read
axes.definition: Large sequential read throughput on warm/resident data, as the workload experiences it.

axes.name: Streaming write
axes.definition: Large sequential write throughput on the application's write path (background publish excluded unless it blocks the app).

axes.name: Small-file / metadata-heavy
axes.definition: Throughput of create/stat/delete storms and many-small-file trees (npm install, untar, large clones).

axes.name: Hot-loop local I/O
axes.definition: Latency-sensitive synchronous loops — sqlite transactions, git operations, build dirs, agent scratch — where per-op latency, not bandwidth, paces the tool.

axes.name: Cold start / first access
axes.definition: Time from pod start (or first access after idle/eviction) to a usable, hot workspace.

axes.name: Scale-out ceiling
axes.definition: How aggregate throughput grows as client/pod count grows, and what shared component caps it.

cells.rationale: Measured: 512 MiB sequential read 164 MB/s vs 147 MB/s local (1.1x) — 'Streaming is fine; metadata is the constraint' (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'What it performs like'). Competitive per client, but the wire and the hub's single NIC cap it where local NVMe would not.

Design estimate, dormant: the tree's only Kerberos mention is a 'dormant pure-Rust RPCSEC_GSS/Kerberos implementation (krb5/krb5i/krb5p)' (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-113). Privacy mode decrypts every READ payload per RPC on both ends; the docs do not quantify it, so scored qualitatively below sys's measured 164 MB/s.

As designed (not built): 'your subtree — full local POSIX at disk speed' for resident files (flint-fuse-architecture.html p3), but 'v1 ships the classic daemon data path' with passthrough/io-uring 'opportunistic accelerators only' — every read byte transits the userspace daemon.
'PLAIN FILES — a real local filesystem, full POSIX, zero interception' (flint-lean-architecture.html); reads come from the node's own disk and page cache with nothing of flint's in the path.
Measured: 512 MiB sequential write 104 MB/s vs 173 MB/s local — 0.6x (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'What it performs like' table).

Design estimate, dormant: krb5p wraps every WRITE payload in per-message GSS encryption on the client and the hub's pure-Rust GSS path (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-113); unquantified in the docs, so scored qualitatively below sys's measured 0.6x-of-local.

As designed: writes land on the emptyDir working set ('capture intervals, durable bit, pre-ack', flint-fuse-architecture.html p3) — local speed minus the classic-FUSE copy path; the 8-13 s/GiB publish rate (p4 RPO arithmetic) is background and never blocks the app's write.

The app writes plain local files with zero interception; publish is an asynchronous cadence scan measured at 8.0 s/GiB sidecar-side floor that sits outside the write path (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md bytes axis).

Measured: create 12.5x slower (123/s), delete 222x slower — 'Creating and deleting are not cacheable — each is a synchronous round trip — and that is what dominates the tools agents actually run'; the guide's own advice is to move this work off the mount onto emptyDir (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md).

The same synchronous per-op round trips, each additionally GSS-wrapped and unwrapped; dormant and unquantified (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-113), so scored as designed, strictly below sys's measured 12.5x/222x cliff.

Design estimate: own-subtree create/delete are local daemon ops with no network RTT ('full local POSIX at disk speed', flint-fuse-architecture.html p3), but each op is a user-kernel FUSE transition plus a capture note and state.db row ('one note*() from every mutating op'); never measured.

Storms hit the local filesystem natively; the measured 100k-file leg shows the cost surfacing only in the background barrier (117 s first publish, 2.8 s idle tick, 27 MiB manifest), not in app-facing op latency (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md file-count axis).

'npm install, a build tree, or git clone of a large repository will be paced by create/delete, not by bandwidth' — the guide tells you to run exactly this shape on local scratch (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md); sqlite/git are correct through the mount but every lock/fsync/commit is a network round trip.
Same RTT pacing plus per-message GSS crypto on each of those small synchronous RPCs; dormant in-tree, overhead unquantified — scored as the designed posture (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-113).

As designed: single-pod sqlite/git run on the local working set at 'disk speed' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p3), with fsync-heavy loops still paying per-op daemon transitions; cross-pod shared sqlite/git is refused with errno and routed to the hub (the death list) — a scoping choice, not a slowdown.

Proven with real binaries on the rig: 'git fsck --strict clean... sqlite integrity_check ok, all rows present' on plain local files across 3 publish barriers — the loop itself is never intercepted (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md e2e leg).

Best per-pod story in the field: the working set persists on the hub's PVC, so agent pod churn pays only a mount; a suspended share woke and served in a measured 11 s floor, can exceed 25 s (flint-hub-gateway.md 'Waking'); the bad cases are Hibernated (full DR import, 'times out by design') and evicted files at a measured 131 s/GiB single-stream, divided by the default fan-out of 6 (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'Hydration from S3').

Same PVC-warm hub machinery, plus GSS context establishment in the mount path — 'KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd' (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-113) — an added first-access dependency; dormant, design estimate.

Boot 'imports manifest stubs, no bytes moved' — fastest time-to-first-file — but each touched byte pays hydration: 72.5 s/GiB measured pre-fan-out, and the doc's own gate says measuring hydrate with fan-out 'decides whether per-pod cold start is viable at all'; 1000-pod correlated starts risk 503 storms (flint-fuse-architecture.html p3, p5 gates). Designed, not built.

'cold start downloads the whole workspace; fine at GiB scale' (flint-lean-architecture.html); measured floor 3.3 s/GiB and 49.5 s for 100k files on a sequential loopback loop (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md) — every pod start pays the full checkout, and the checkout fan-out is a named lever not yet built.

'Not a parallel filesystem. One hub is one pod and one NIC. If a single pod's bandwidth is your ceiling, the full pNFS profile...' (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'What this is not') — every client's bytes aggregate into one pod's NIC.

The same one-pod, one-NIC ceiling, and the hub's CPU must additionally GSS-wrap/unwrap every byte for every client, so the aggregate cap arrives at whichever of NIC or crypto CPU saturates first; unquantified in docs — design estimate on the dormant implementation (pnfs-operator-runbook.md).

No hub in the data plane — 'the only always-on component is S3 itself' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p1); throughput scales with pods against S3, bounded only by the bucket (503 SlowDown under correlated bursts; 'N uncoordinated engines, N x re-fetch of the same objects' is the duplication tax, p4).

Grade 2 gateway: 'bytes go pod -> S3 DIRECT' with presigned PUTs; the gateway is a stateless N-replica control plane and 'reads never depended on it' (flint-lean-architecture.html) — aggregate scales with pods to S3's own limits. Built through Phase 3.

proposal.note: This chart is the consistency chart inverted: the direct modes dominate every hot-path axis because their data path is local — Lean's zero-interception plain files sweep streaming, small-file, and hot-loop I/O, while the hub's measured metadata cliff (create 12.5x, delete 222x slower) is sec=sys's worst cell. The hub's one genuine win is cold start: its PVC-persistent working set means agent pod churn pays only a mount, where Lean re-downloads the whole workspace every pod start and FUSE's 72.5 s/GiB pre-fan-out hydrate is still gated on a viability measurement. krb5p trails sec=sys on all six axes — GSS privacy encrypts every RPC payload byte, an overhead the docs never quantify (scored as designed; the implementation is dormant in-tree). Scale-out is the structural split: one hub is one pod and one NIC, while both direct modes stream pod-to-S3 and scale with the fleet.

verdicts.reason: Measured table verified in flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'What it performs like': read 164 MB/s vs 147 MB/s local, 1.1x, and 'Streaming is fine; metadata is the constraint.' Per-client the wire is competitive with local disk, but warm data still crosses one NIC where FUSE (warm local cache, 4) and Lean (plain local files, 5) serve locally — the 3.5 slot half a point under FUSE is the defensible relative placement. No doc evidence found that it is too high or too low.

Table verified: write 104 MB/s vs 173 MB/s local, 0.6x (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md). A 0.6x measured app-path write against FUSE/Lean whose app-path writes land on local disk (background publish excluded by the axis definition) supports 3 vs 4/5; the half-point drop below the read score matches the measured 1.1x-read vs 0.6x-write asymmetry.

Verified: create 16,172 ms (123/s) = 12.5x slower, delete 8,007 ms vs 36 ms = 222x slower; 'Creating and deleting are not cacheable — each is a synchronous round trip — and that is what dominates the tools agents actually run', plus the guide's own emptyDir-for-node_modules advice (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md). Brutal enough to argue for 1, but stat is only 1.3x slower (attribute caching works) and krb5p — the same round trips plus per-RPC GSS wrapping — must sit strictly below at 1, so 1.5 is the coherent relative slot.

Verified: 'npm install, a build tree, or git clone of a large repository will be paced by create/delete, not by bandwidth' and 'Do small-file-heavy work on local scratch, persist artifacts' (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md). sqlite/git are functional through the mount (fixed in 934ae78 per repo history) but every sync op is a wire round trip; 2 sits correctly between small-files 1.5 (create/delete storms, the worst case) and streaming 3, and two full points under FUSE whose hot loops hit local disk.

Verified in flint-hub-gateway.md 'Waking': IdleSuspended share 'came back and served the request in 11s' read 'as a floor', both bad paths 'can exceed 25s', and 'A Hibernated share is a full DR import from the bucket and will time out here by design'; hydration measured 'byte-identical in 131 s' for 1 GiB single-stream with default fan-out 6 (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md). The differentiator holds against the field: the hub PVC's cache is shared and survives agent pod churn (a new pod pays only a mount), whereas flint-fuse-architecture.html shows per-pod 'lazy hydrate on first touch — 8 MiB x fan-out' (cold cache per pod) and flint-lean-architecture.html requires 'checkout at start — the import' (full subtree download per pod). sys 4 > FUSE 3.5 > Lean 3 survives.

Quote verified: 'Not a parallel filesystem. One hub is one pod and one NIC. If a single pod's bandwidth is your ceiling, the full pNFS profile speaks the same protocol... graduating is adding data servers, not migrating' (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'What this is not'). Every client's aggregate bytes funnel through one pod, versus FUSE/Lean at 4.5 where each pod talks to S3 directly; krb5p at 1 (same NIC plus GSS crypto on the hub CPU) leaves 1.5 as the correct relative floor-adjacent slot. The pNFS graduation path is a different profile, not this approach, so it cannot raise the score.

No doc quantifies krb5p, so the cell is necessarily qualitative; the direction and size hold up. Every READ payload is GSS-privacy-wrapped per RPC, and the in-tree implementation (spdk-csi-driver/src/nfs/kerberos.rs) is AES-CTS-HMAC-SHA1 with hand-rolled ciphertext stealing plus per-message HMAC-SHA1 — heavier per byte than modern AEAD — on both the hub and the kernel client. Against sys's measured 164 MB/s / 1.1x-local read (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md 'What it performs like'), a 1.5-point drop expressing roughly-half-or-worse streaming throughput is defensible, and I found no doc claim pushing it higher or lower.

Symmetric with the read cell: sys write is already 0.6x local (104 MB/s, flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md), and krb5p adds per-message AES-CTS+HMAC-SHA1 wrap on the client and unwrap on the hub for every WRITE payload (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117; kerberos.rs). The -1.5 delta matches the read-axis delta, keeping the series internally consistent. No doc evidence refutes 1.5.

I tried to refute this upward using the guide's own claim that 'each is a synchronous round trip — and that is what dominates' (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md) — implying crypto adds little per 4KiB op and krb5p could equal sys's 1.5. But krb5p is strictly worse on every one of those round trips (per-message GSS wrap/unwrap plus gssd context liveness in the path), sys is already near the floor at 1.5 from the measured 12.5x/222x cliff, and 0.5 is the minimum expressible penalty. That counter is a granularity quibble, not a doc refutation, so 1 stands.

Same structure as small-files: the pacing is per-op RTT (sys measured create 8ms/op class), krb5p adds per-message crypto and GSS sequence handling to each synchronous RPC, and the -0.5 from sys's 2 mirrors the -0.5 on the small-file axis, keeping the two RTT-paced axes consistent. Dormant and unquantified in docs (pnfs-operator-runbook.md is the only mention), so the minimal strict penalty is the defensible call.

The hub machinery is identical to sys (PVC-warm, no hydration difference), and the only added first-access cost is GSS context establishment plus its dependencies — 'KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd, sec=krb5p mount opts' (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~113-115) — a real new dependency in the mount path (KDC reachability, credential acquisition) but sub-second when healthy. -0.5 from sys's 4 is exactly the minimal penalty for an added dependency; nothing in the docs supports a larger or zero delta.

I tried the 'NIC caps both equally, so krb5p should tie sys at 1.5' refutation and it fails: the hub is one pod with one NIC (flint-lite-architecture.html single-hub design; measured rig is a 2-vCPU i4i.large per flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md), and the dormant GSS path is software AES-CTS+HMAC-SHA1 (kerberos.rs) that must wrap/unwrap every byte for every client on the hub's CPU — so the aggregate cap plausibly arrives at crypto CPU before the NIC. Strictly-below-sys at 1 is correct; both are floor-adjacent versus FUSE/Lean at 4.5 whose data planes fan out to S3 directly.

4 survives. Resident reads are 'full local POSIX at disk speed' (p3 contract box) but 'v1 ships the classic daemon data path' with passthrough/io-uring as 'opportunistic accelerators only' (p3, line: 'passthrough routes writes around the daemon and silently breaks capture completeness') — every byte transits userspace, justifying exactly the 1-point gap below Lean's zero-interception plain files. Above sys=3.5 is right: hub read is a network NFS path (measured 164 MB/s, ~1.1x that rig's local disk, fleets guide) while FUSE reads local emptyDir. No doc evidence puts FUSE at or below sys, nor at parity with Lean.

4 survives an active attack: the CR's dirtySetCapGiB: 10 (p2) plus 'refusals block in-handler' (p3) means a sustained stream past ~10 GiB dirty would block at publish rate (8-13 s/GiB ~ the hub's measured 104 MB/s), but p5 explicitly routes 'large-artifact writers (dirty > ~10 GiB)' to the hub, so within FUSE's designed envelope the ack is 'durable to the pod's emptyDir... local-disk latency' (consistency doc) and the figcaption claims 'lower write latency than NFS'. Below Lean's 5 (no interception, no cap, nothing can ever block the app) and above sys's 3 (0.6x local measured) is the right ordering with the right gaps.

3.5 survives. Own-subtree creates/deletes have no network RTT (vs the hub's measured 12.5x-slower create / 222x-slower delete, flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md), but each mutation pays a FUSE transition plus 'one note*() from every mutating op' with the 'dirty bit written pre-ack' into state.db (p3 + consistency doc) — a real per-op durability write Lean's scan-based publish never pays on the op path. One caveat found: 'O_EXCL create → sync If-None-Match:* PUT' (death list) puts an S3 RTT on O_EXCL creates, but untar/npm/clone storms are ordinary creates. 3.5 — well above sys 1.5, a full 1.5 below Lean's native 5, never measured — is calibrated correctly.

4 survives the strongest refutation attempt in this set: the death list's unqualified 'fcntl byte-range locks → ENOLCK' and 'shared-writable mmap → refused' would break even single-pod sqlite if read flatly. But every statement of the contract qualifies it — 'cross-pod locks, shared sqlite, shared git: refused with errno' (p1), 'no cross-pod locks, no shared sqlite / git' (flint-fuse-consistency.html), 'multi-pod sqlite/git' (p4 figcaption) — and the consistency figcaption states 'inside your subtree, flint-fuse is a local filesystem — lower write latency than NFS' with fsync at 'local-disk latency'. That directly supports FUSE >> sys=2 (measured ~8 ms per sync metadata op on the hub) and < Lean=5 (no daemon transitions, native fcntl/mmap). Residual sqlite-WAL mmap ambiguity is not concrete enough to defeat the half-step structure.

3.5 survives attacks from both directions. Down: 'the price: every pod start is a Hibernated-class cold start' (p2 fleet math), hydrate 'measured pre-fan-out' at 72.5 s/GiB with the p5 gate saying fan-out measurement 'decides whether per-pod cold start is viable at all', 1000-pod 503-storm risk, and a '60s configured, 80-110s measured' write lockout after unclean predecessor death (p4). Up: 'import manifest stubs, no bytes moved' (p3 boot strip) gives the fastest time-to-first-file of any approach, and touched-fraction workloads beat Lean's mandatory whole-workspace checkout ('cold start downloads the whole workspace', lean p1). Sitting between sys=4 (warm hub: mount and serve, data hot on the PVC) and Lean=3 is the defensible middle; the proposer already discounted for the unproven viability gate.

4.5 survives. 'the only always-on component is S3 itself' (p1) and 'mode: direct — NOTHING standing... zero pods, zero Services, zero PVCs' (p2) remove every shared flint component from the data plane — a category above sys/krb5p's single-hub NIC ceiling (1.5/1). The half-point off 5 is exactly what p4 documents: 'N uncoordinated engines, N x re-fetch of the same objects' under throttle storms, boot-wave 503 SlowDown against an unpartitioned bucket (p3), and per-pod duplication so large that 'per-NODE mount pods... the largest single lever on every duplication term' (p5) exists as an escalation. These are efficiency and burst taxes, not a shared throughput cap, so 4.5 rather than lower; parity with Lean at 4.5 is fair since lean's recorded decision (commit 93d691f, grade-1 proxy primary) puts lean bytes through a gateway that 'pays back a slice of the hub's NIC ceiling' (lean p1) while FUSE pods go pod-to-S3 direct.

'PLAIN FILES — a real local filesystem, full POSIX, zero interception' (flint-lean-architecture.html) is unambiguous: warm reads are node-local disk/page cache with no flint component in the path. Searched for refuting evidence — the sidecar scan is background (2.8 s idle tick at 100k files, flint-lean-0b-measurements.md) and touches no read op. Relative to FUSE=4 (userspace daemon in every read), 5 is the correct top of column.

App writes hit local files unintercepted; publish is 'publish at cadence — mtime/size scan against the manifest' (flint-lean-architecture.html) and the measured 8.0 s/GiB is sidecar-side (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md). Checked the candidate refuters: preStop barrier gates pod termination not app writes; publish amplification (plan §6) and dirtySetCapGiB are background/economics terms; emptyDir budget is capacity, not throughput. Zero interception means flint structurally cannot pace the app's write path — 5 vs FUSE's 4 holds.

Create/stat/delete storms run on native local ext4; the measured 100k-file leg puts all cost in the background barrier (117 s first publish, 2.8 s no-change walk, 27 MiB manifest — flint-lean-0b-measurements.md), and even the 1M-entry worry the doc raises (~283 MB manifest CAS per changed barrier) is publish-path, not app-facing op latency. No doc evidence puts anything of flint's in an app metadata op. 5 vs FUSE=3.5 is correctly calibrated.

Proven, not just designed: the 0b e2e leg ran real git + sqlite on plain local files across 3 barriers — 'git fsck --strict clean... sqlite integrity_check ok, all rows present' (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md). Per-op latency is local-filesystem latency; the only residuals found (empty dirs don't round-trip, torn-hot-file under forced barrier — plan §3) are durability/fidelity items, not loop latency. 5 confirmed.

The refutation evidence cuts both ways and does not defeat 3. Against: full-download start gate is mandatory ('agent cannot start before checkout-complete', flint-lean-plan.md §2.4), the 3.3 s/GiB / 49.5 s numbers are disclaimed FLOOR numbers on a sequential loop, 'the hub's 600 s default kills a 20 GiB checkout at the only measured rate', and gateway/proxy down means 'starting pods wedge' (§7). For: the axis targets a usable HOT workspace — lean's checkout ends fully hot local, whereas FUSE's lazy hydration (3.5) is usable-but-cold per first access and sys (4) is never local-hot. Bottom-of-column 3 already prices the pay-everything-upfront posture.

The rationale rests on grade-2 ('bytes go pod → S3 DIRECT', 'reads never depended on it') but the plan of record decided against it: 'Proxy posture (decided): grade-1 primary' (docs/plans/flint-lean-plan.md §2.2) and 'Presigned grade-2 (un-deferred only by a measured 0c proxy bottleneck)' (§8 explicit deferrals); §6 adds 'Checkout: full-workspace GET per pod start through the proxy'. So EVERY publish and checkout byte transits the proxy tier, whose own Phase 0c acceptance names 'the BINDING constraint: sustained GB/s per proxy replica (both NIC directions)' with checkout admission so bursts queue (§5); §7's corrected failure model supersedes the arch page's 'reads never depended on it' with 'checkouts/restarts wedge'. As-built matches grade-1: no presign code exists in /Users/ddalton/github/flint/lean/sidecar/src/. FUSE is bucket-direct ('agents and the project service reach S3 directly', flint-fuse-architecture.html) with nothing below S3, so a 4.5 tie is unsupportable; the horizontally-sizable proxy formula ceil(N×W×2/(T×replica_GBps)) keeps lean far above the hub approaches — 4.0, half a point under FUSE.

axes.name: Client authentication strength
axes.definition: How strongly a writer must prove who it is before the store or server accepts its operations.

axes.name: Wire protection
axes.definition: Confidentiality and integrity of data and control traffic in transit.

axes.name: Unauthenticated DoS resistance
axes.definition: How little a merely-reachable, credential-less peer can do to exhaust memory, state, or availability.

axes.name: Tenancy isolation
axes.definition: Strength and enforceability of the boundary that keeps one tenant/project from reading or writing another's data.

axes.name: Pod-compromise blast radius
axes.definition: How little an attacker who owns an agent pod gains (credentials, privileges, forgeable identity) and how fast that gain can be revoked - higher = smaller, faster-contained blast.

axes.name: Misconfiguration resistance
axes.definition: Whether the security posture fails closed and survives operator error - secure defaults, unforgeable second layers, refusal over silent degradation.

cells.rationale: "Port 2049 is AUTH_SYS: the client asserts its own uid and the server takes it" (flint-lite-architecture.html), and B9 records "AUTH_SYS trusts wire uid 0, no squash, no in-process authz" (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md) - identity is self-declared, not proven.

Per-user cryptographic proof: "a dormant pure-Rust RPCSEC_GSS/Kerberos implementation (krb5/krb5i/krb5p, keytab via KRB5_KTNAME)... the documented strong-auth path" (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:109-113). Scored as designed - the code is in-tree but dormant, validated only via pynfs --security=krb5, never production-wired.

SigV4/IRSA machine identity, unforgeable at the store: "every pod holds prefix-scoped credentials (IRSA, token mounted in the sidecar container only)" and "IAM principal tags enforce it independently" (flint-fuse-architecture.html). Strong proof, but workload-granular, not per-user - and designed, not built.

Bearer at the gateway shipped in Phase 3 ("bearer + revocation", flint-lean-plan.md Phase 3; a602e08), with grade-2 grants "pinned to exactly those keys" (flint-lean-architecture.html) so authority is key-exact; but "Auth v1: bearer only vs + SigV4 - open" and per-workspace bearers are still owed (flint-lean-plan.md §9.3, status header) - a bearer is a weaker proof than SigV4 signing.

Cleartext RPC: the runbook is explicit that the shipped posture gives "no per-user authentication or wire encryption" (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:108-109); RPC-with-TLS (xprtsec=mtls) is only "attractive once client kernels reach >= 6.5".

krb5p is per-message GSS privacy plus integrity on every NFS RPC, mutually authenticated - the strongest wire posture in the tree (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:109-113) - but it is the dormant path, scored as designed.

All data-plane traffic is S3 over TLS to the bucket endpoint - "plain S3, no flint server anywhere in the read path" (flint-lean-architecture.html page 2, covering direct-mode FUSE and lean alike); no cleartext NFS hop exists in this design.
Every hop is HTTPS: sidecar to proxy/gateway bearer-authed TLS, and grade-2 presigned PUT/GET "bytes go pod -> S3 DIRECT" over TLS (flint-lean-architecture.html); same TLS-everywhere posture as FUSE.

The B5-B8 class is fixed at HEAD - state-table quota ("any TCP-reachable peer mints unbounded clients/sessions/stateids/lock rows", B6, fixed 66474e8), slot-cache cap (996a929), idle-socket deadline (B7, 56e8d2c), READ clamp (B8, aad7a47) - but the surface remains a full stateful NFSv4.1 machine on an open port where "no credential needed" (B7) to engage it; the defense is caps, not auth.

Same server, same port, same B5-B8 fixes and the same pre-auth TCP/session surface; the hardening plan's DoS findings (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md B5-B8) predate any GSS gating, and no doc claims GSS shrinks the floodable surface - scored equal to sys.

There is no flint-operated door to flood: "no hub... the store's own CAS" (flint-fuse-architecture.html) - the reachable data plane is S3 itself, which refuses unsigned requests; the only cluster service is a create-time webhook, not a data path.

The gateway is stateless ("N replicas... no PVC, no epoch of its own, no state") and even a successful DoS only pauses publishes: "gateway down => publishes pause... far softer than hub-down; reads never depended on it" (flint-lean-architecture.html). Docked half a point vs FUSE because a flint-run door exists and has had no B5-B8-style hardening battery (Phase 0c burst rig still open, flint-lean-plan.md).

"no auth on 2049 - the network is the boundary" and "nfsClientCIDRs cannot express a client in another cluster" (flint-lite-architecture.html, flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md:732), NetworkPolicy "defaults off and is documented-vacuous cross-cluster" (B9); plus B12 prefix-reuse adoption "open at HEAD... B serves A's files, no race required" (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md B12).

Proven per-user identity finally makes POSIX modes bind to a real principal instead of a self-declared uid (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:108-113), but the tenancy machinery around it is unchanged - same per-prefix hubs, same open-at-HEAD B12 adoption hole, same network-shaped cross-cluster boundary.

"IAM scope ends at ws-a/" with principal-tag conditions as "a second, unforgeable layer", and the two-principal split keeps bucket-wide levers (PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration, "a bucket-wide delete lever") out of workspace policies (flint-fuse-architecture.html). Store-side and unforgeable, but designed-only, and it obliges the engine to regain its server-side Prefix on upload listing.

"Proxy tenancy: project-granular, dedicated bucket or prefix per project (DECIDED). Cross-project isolation proxy-native" (flint-lean-plan.md §9.6), plus claim identity with foreign-on-reused-prefix refusal arms ("foreign-on-reused-prefix must refuse", flint-lean-plan.md Phase 1) closing the B12 class; "within-project residual accepted for v1 (versioning recovers)" keeps it off 4.5.

The pod holds no secrets, but any compromised pod that can reach 2049 "can claim any uid" with "no root-squash" (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md:714,690) - i.e. root on every reachable share - and there is no per-client credential to revoke; the only cut-off lever is network isolation. One saving grace: bucket creds stay in the hub ("the bucket trusts one principal: the hub").

A compromised pod yields only that user's short-lived ticket - keytabs live on nodes, not pods ("KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd", pnfs-operator-runbook.md:111) - and the KDC can disable the principal; blast is bounded to one authenticated identity. Scored as designed; the dormant path has never been production-drilled.

The doc concedes it: prefix-scoped creds narrow cross-tenant reach "while irreducibly widening what a compromised pod can do to its own subtree, .flint/ cells included, because flint-fuse itself is the epoch holder" - and the same pod carries a "privileged · Bidirectional · /dev/fuse" sidecar that PSA baseline/restricted refuse, so a sidecar compromise reaches the node, and "a flint-fuse CVE reaches the fleet by pod churn" (flint-fuse-architecture.html). IRSA revocation is IAM-propagation slow, not seconds.

"pods hold ZERO bucket write credentials", the sidecar is an "ordinary process - UNPRIVILEGED, no /dev/fuse... no PSA conflict", and "revocation in seconds - kill the token" with per-request epoch validation refusing deposed writers (flint-lean-architecture.html; flint-lean-plan.md §2.2). Caveat noted: as built through Phase 3 the sidecar still CASes cells directly through its project-scoped proxy token by default (plan status header), so the enforced-arbitration half is design-forward.

The flagship footgun fails open and silent: "sec=sys is not optional, and leaving it out fails quietly... gives every agent root on the share" (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md:692-702), NetworkPolicy defaults off (B9), and listing remote CIDRs "denies the address the traffic actually comes from" - the safe configuration is documentation-enforced only.

Kerberos misconfiguration at least fails closed (an unwired mount refuses rather than granting root), but the path is dormant, "validated via pynfs --security=krb5" only (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:112-113), and KDC/per-node-keytab/rpc.gssd wiring is the classic sprawl with zero in-tree tooling - the widest gap between designed and operable posture on this chart.

Defense-in-depth is designed in: "The webhook must not be the security boundary... IAM principal-tag conditions enforce the same mapping independently - a forged pod annotation buys nothing, and a webhook bug is caught by a second, unforgeable layer", with failurePolicy: Fail mandated because "Ignore is worse than an outage" (flint-fuse-architecture.html). Docked for the bootstrap footgun (prefix-scoped policy 403s engine startup until a pre-bootstrapped mode exists) and stale-sidecar exposure.

Refusal over detection everywhere: "the gateway is the enforcement point these cells always lacked - detection becomes refusal" (flint-lean-architecture.html), the shared token plumbing mounts "no routes at all without one - 404, not 401" and the chart "refuses to render" on credential misconfig (file-api-fleet-auth.md; flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md:82), and the proxy conformance gate has must-FAIL arms "refusing barriers while drifted" (flint-lean-plan.md §2.2) - fail-closed by construction, though Phase 4 operator/webhook is unbuilt.

proposal.note: Security is where the four approaches diverge hardest: sec=sys is bottom-of-chart on five of six axes because identity is self-asserted, the wire is cleartext, and the boundary is reachability ("nfsClientCIDRs cannot express a client in another cluster"). krb5p buys the strongest auth and wire on a dormant, never-wired code path, and pays for it on misconfiguration resistance. The sharpest contrast is blast radius vs everything else: FUSE wins tenancy isolation with unforgeable IAM yet craters on pod compromise (creds in every pod plus a privileged /dev/fuse sidecar), while Lean holds the best overall envelope - zero pod write credentials, seconds-scale revocation, unprivileged sidecar. DoS resistance, promoted to its own axis, shows the NFS door quota-hardened at HEAD (B5-B8 fixed) but still a stateful surface caps defend rather than auth.

verdicts.reason: AUTH_SYS remains self-declared identity at HEAD: 'Port 2049 is AUTH_SYS: the client asserts its own uid and the server takes it' (flint-lite-architecture.html). The a8a1f5a flavor-order fix changes which flavor is negotiated, not the strength of the flavor itself — the credential is still an unauthenticated uid assertion. 0.5 rather than 0 is defensible because POSIX modes are now genuinely enforced against the asserted uid (906674c 'check permissions against the CALLER', authz failures 265->4), a notch above nothing; the 4-point gap to krb5p's cryptographic per-user identity is correctly calibrated.

Cleartext NFS RPC as shipped: 'What this does NOT give you: per-user authentication or wire encryption' (pnfs-operator-runbook.md, the passage right before the dormant RPCSEC_GSS note); RPC-with-TLS is only prospective ('xprtsec=mtls ... becomes attractive once client kernels reach >= 6.5'). 0.5 rather than 0 is fair since the hub-to-S3 write-back leg rides HTTPS, but every NFS byte between client and hub is plaintext with no integrity protection. Confirmed.

Verified in git log that the whole class landed: B5 slot cache (996a929), B6 state-table quota (66474e8 'any peer could mint clients, stateids, and locks without bound'), B7 idle deadline (56e8d2c 'an idle socket held its capped slot forever'), B8 READ clamp (aad7a47) — the proposer's fix inventory is accurate, and 2.5 correctly reflects that the surface is still a full stateful NFSv4.1 machine on an open port where 'no credential needed' (B7, nfs-server-hardening-plan.md line 93): with caps but no auth, a reachable peer can still fill the capped connection/state budget and deny legitimate clients. Mid-scale versus FUSE's no-listening-surface 4.5 holds.

Every cited claim verified at HEAD: 'no auth on 2049 — the network is the boundary' (flint-lite-architecture.html); 'nfsClientCIDRs cannot express a client in another cluster' with the measured 1486/1486 SNAT capture, and 'hubNamespaces defaults to []' so enabling the policy guards no hub (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md ~714-744); B12 'open at HEAD ... B serves A's files, no race required' (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md line 98) — hub-side tenant adoption on prefix reuse is a live data-exposure hole. No compensating layer exists; 0.5 stands.

Verified at HEAD: authz.rs:40 states 'uid 0 is honoured as root, i.e. no_root_squash' and B9's remediation defers squash/allow-list to 'post-GA' (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md line 95), so a compromised pod that reaches 2049 is root on every reachable share with no per-client credential to revoke — containment is network surgery only. The saving grace the proposer credits ('the bucket trusts one principal: the hub', flint-lite-architecture.html) is real and is what keeps this at 1 rather than 0.5; the ordering below FUSE's 1.5 (attacker there gains actual but scoped S3 creds) is defensible.

The proposer's headline evidence is stale as-shipped. Commit a8a1f5a (Aug 24) fixed the flagship footgun: SECINFO now advertises 'AUTH_SYS — first: carries a uid to check' with 'AUTH_NONE — LAST' (verified in code, spdk-csi-driver/src/nfs/v4/compound.rs:2083-2092), the commit records 'a stock mount -t nfs -o vers=4.1 ... The same mount now negotiates sec=sys', pins the order with a unit test, and explicitly flags the quoted agent-fleets-guide passage as describing pre-fix behavior ('It was not advice'). B9's 'no in-process authz' is also closed (906674c, authz failures 265->4 with 0 over-denials; CI gate 6ce9a38 on a real mount). So the secure-defaults half of this axis materially improved: omitting sec=sys no longer silently grants root. What keeps it at 1.5, not higher: the enforceable boundary still fails open silently — NetworkPolicy defaults off with hubNamespaces=[] vacuous enablement, CNIs that 'ignore NetworkPolicy in silence', cross-cluster CIDRs that deny the wrong address (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md), and B12's silent tenant adoption open at HEAD — so it stays below krb5p's fail-closed credential layer at 2.

The mechanism is the strongest in the tree, but the design never gates acceptance on it. The runbook's entire wiring list is client/KDC-side — "wiring it up (KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd, sec=krb5p mount opts)" (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:110-111) — and the shipped server accepts AUTH_UNIX unconditionally alongside GSS (spdk-csi-driver/src/nfs/server_v4.rs:733 branches to GSS only when the caller offers it; no export security-flavor policy or FLINT_* knob exists anywhere under src/nfs/). So even a perfectly wired krb5p deployment leaves the self-declared-uid door open next to the strong path — the axis is what a writer MUST prove before acceptance, and here the floor stays AUTH_SYS. Additionally, per-principal state binding was advertised but "do[es] not exist" — the B10 fix (bc7fed3, nfs-server-hardening-plan.md:96) clamped the advertisement rather than implementing the binding. The proposer's 4.5 discounts only dormancy; the missing acceptance-side enforcement is a second, independent shave. 4.0 keeps krb5p clearly above the unconditionally-enforced-but-per-pod peers (FUSE/Lean 3.5: IAM SigV4 / gateway tokens with no unauthenticated path to the store, but pod-granular identity) on per-user, mutual, per-message strength.

Per-message GSS privacy + integrity on every NFS RPC, mutually authenticated (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:109-113), protects the tenants' own traffic even though an attacker may elect cleartext AUTH_SYS for their own session — that hole is an auth/misconfig fact, not exposure of protected traffic. Parity at 4.5 with FUSE/Lean (TLS to S3, gateway HTTPS) is right: krb5p's per-message mutual wrapping is offset by its being a dormant homegrown pure-Rust GSS validated only "via pynfs --security=krb5" (runbook:112-113), versus production rustls/S3 TLS on the other side; the runbook itself treats RPC-with-TLS (xprtsec=mtls, RFC 9289) as the successor path (runbook:113-114). No doc supports separating the three at 0.5 granularity.

Same binary, same port, same fixes: B5 slot-cache cap (996a929), B6 state-table quotas (66474e8 — "any TCP-reachable peer mints unbounded clients/sessions/stateids... no credential needed", nfs-server-hardening-plan.md:92), B7 idle-read deadline (56e8d2c, landed at HEAD contrary to older notes), B8 READ clamp (aad7a47) all predate and are orthogonal to any GSS gating. No doc claims GSS shrinks the pre-auth surface, and the GSS context-establishment path (rpcsec_gss.rs acceptor, reachable pre-authentication) is itself new credential-less state/CPU, so equal-to-sys at 2.5 is the defensible call in both directions.

2 survives. Per-user proof upgrades within-share POSIX enforcement over sys's "AUTH_SYS trusts wire uid 0, no squash, no in-process authz" (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md:95), justifying the lift from 0.5 — but every tenancy boundary above the uid is unchanged: B12 is open at HEAD ("tier/manifest.rs carries no owner/claim identity; delete share A, create share B on the same prefix ⇒ B serves A's files, no race required", plan:98; no fixing commit in git log), the chart NetworkPolicy is "documented-vacuous cross-cluster" (plan:95), and B10 shows client-state was never principal-bound (bc7fed3 removed the false advertisement rather than adding the binding), so going above 2 toward FUSE 3.5 / Lean 4 (store-enforced prefix/project boundaries) has no doc support.

3.5 survives. The credential a pod can steal is one user's ticket: the durable secrets are "per-node keytabs" obtained via node-level rpc.gssd (pnfs-operator-runbook.md:111), not pod-mounted, and a KDC principal disable revokes centrally — versus sys at 1 where "any client claims any uid" against the whole share, and FUSE at 1.5 where "every pod holds prefix-scoped credentials (IRSA, token mounted in the sidecar container only)" (flint-fuse-architecture.html:227). Staying 1 below Lean's 4.5 is also right: lean pods "hold ZERO bucket write credentials" with "revocation in seconds — kill the token" (flint-lean-architecture.html:145,148) — strictly less to steal than one live Kerberos identity. Dormancy/never-drilled is already noted in the rationale.

2 survives, but on narrower grounds than the proposer states: the fail-closed property is client-side only (a sec=krb5p mount refuses rather than degrading), while the server side fails open — the shipped acceptor takes AUTH_UNIX alongside GSS with no refusal policy (server_v4.rs:733; no knob in src/nfs/), and the documented wiring (runbook:110-111) includes no server-side enforcement step, so a client that forgets the mount option silently gets self-declared-uid access. That evidence caps the score at 2 (refutes anything nearer FUSE 3.5 / Lean 4) but does not push below it: the client-side refusal plus KDC-central control is one real fail-closed layer sys entirely lacks at 1, and the operational sprawl ("KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd" with zero in-tree tooling, validated only via pynfs) is already priced into the proposer's number.

Quotes verified in flint-fuse-architecture.html: 'every pod holds bucket credentials — prefix-scoped IAM, sidecar-only token placement' (p.1) and 'derived from namespace + ServiceAccount, never a pod annotation; IAM principal tags enforce it independently' (p.2). Store-verified SigV4/IRSA workload identity sits correctly a full point under krb5p's per-user cryptographic identity (4.5) and far above AUTH_SYS's asserted uids (0.5). I tried to push FUSE above Lean (IRSA beats Lean v1's bearer-only auth — flint-lean-plan.md §9.3 'Auth v1: bearer only vs + SigV4 — open', SigV4/TokenReview deferred in §8), but the designed-not-built dock (git: '63e0e20 FUSE track deprioritized', no FUSE code) offsets it; parity at 3.5 survives.

Verified: 'direct-mode REST access — lean AND FUSE variants alike — is the bucket endpoint: plain S3, no flint server anywhere in the read path' (flint-lean-architecture.html p.2), and the FUSE data plane is SigV4-signed S3 ('publish — If-Match…', 'hydrate on first touch' straight to the bucket, flint-fuse-architecture.html p.1). No cleartext NFS hop exists anywhere in the design, and no doc distinguishes FUSE's transit posture from Lean's or krb5p's — the three-way tie at 4.5 with sys at 0.5 is exactly what the docs support.

Verified: 'the only always-on component is S3 itself' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p.1) and 'mode: direct — NOTHING standing… zero pods, zero Services, zero PVCs' (p.2); the admission webhook is reachable only by the API server, not a credential-less peer. The relative ordering holds against the docs: hub modes carry the B6 unbounded-state-table and B7 slowloris history (nfs-server-hardening-plan.md rows B6/B7, fixes 66474e8/56e8d2c), and Lean stands a reachable gateway+proxy door (flint-lean-architecture.html), so FUSE 4.5 > Lean 4 > hub 2.5 is grounded. The 1000-pod 503-storm and heartbeat-cost material (pp.2-3) is authenticated self-load, not unauthenticated DoS, so it does not defeat the score.

I actively tested whether FUSE should exceed Lean's 4, since 'IAM scope ends at ws-a/' plus principal-tag conditions is workspace-granular and store-enforced while Lean accepts a within-project residual ('Cross-project isolation proxy-native; within-project residual accepted for v1', flint-lean-plan.md §9.6). The refutation fails on the proposer's own cited docks, which I verified: the design is unbuilt (63e0e20), the engine's 'deliberately bucket-wide upload listing… regains its server-side Prefix on real S3' is an owed change, and bootstrap 'refuses startup on the 403 a prefix-scoped policy would hand it' until a pre-bootstrapped mode exists (flint-fuse-architecture.html p.2) — so the workspace-granular IAM story is not yet load-bearing as coded. Lean's built, battery-proven 'pods hold ZERO bucket write credentials' + 'detection becomes refusal' gateway keeps Lean >= FUSE defensible. 3.5 stands.

Tested upward (app container holds no credentials — 'IRSA token mounted here ONLY', skip-containers; IAM contains cross-tenant reach better than sys's forge-any-uid) and downward. The downward evidence dominates and is verbatim in flint-fuse-architecture.html: the sidecar is 'privileged · Bidirectional · /dev/fuse' (node escape reaches every co-scheduled pod's tokens, and PSA baseline/restricted refuse it — the unprivileged broker is only a 'named endgame'); the pod is 'the epoch holder and manifest publisher' so a compromise forges its subtree's .flint/ cells; 'a flint-fuse CVE reaches the fleet by pod churn'; and revocation is IAM-propagation, versus Lean's 'revocation in seconds — kill the token' (flint-lean-architecture.html). Barely above sys's 1 and far below Lean's 4.5 is exactly 1.5.

Verified the defense-in-depth quotes ('The webhook must not be the security boundary… a webhook bug is caught by a second, unforgeable layer'; 'failurePolicy: Ignore — worse than an outage'; declared-volumeMount belt-and-braces plus the verify-pass black-hole detector, flint-fuse-architecture.html p.2). I looked for evidence forcing it lower and found two additional footguns beyond the proposer's — 'bucket Versioning is a HARD requirement in this mode — it is the only recovery window CAS cannot provide' (p.1), and the privileged recipe's PSA collision inviting policy loosening — but these are the same class the proposer already docked for (bootstrap 403, stale sidecars), and the second-unforgeable-IAM-layer design keeps it clearly above krb5p's 2 while Lean's simpler recipe ('webhook injection shrinks to: an emptyDir + an ordinary sidecar') justifies Lean at 4 above it. 3.5 survives.

Cannot equal FUSE's 3.5. FUSE's score rests on per-pod cloud-issued SigV4/IRSA — 'IRSA token mounted here ONLY', 'IAM principal tags enforce it independently — a forged pod annotation buys nothing... a second, unforgeable layer' (flint-fuse-architecture.html). Lean's decided-and-built proof of identity is a static bearer that is not even per-workspace: 'Auth v1: bearer only vs + SigV4 — open' (flint-lean-plan.md §9.3), 'SigV4 pod identity / TokenReview at the gateway' is an explicit §8 deferral, and the status header lists 'per-workspace bearers/SigV4' still open. The proposer's counterweight — grants 'pinned to exactly those keys' — is authorization granularity, not authentication strength, and belongs to grade-2, which §8 defers ('grade-1 primary', §2.2). On an axis defined as how strongly a writer proves who it is, a shared replayable bearer sits below per-pod cryptographic request signing: 3.0.

The rationale's central evidence is misread twice. (1) No lean doc claims TLS anywhere — grep over flint-lean-architecture.html and flint-lean-plan.md finds zero TLS/HTTPS/encryption mentions; the 'over TLS' attribution is the proposer's, not the doc's. (2) 'bytes go pod → S3 DIRECT' describes grade-2 presigned, which is DEFERRED: 'Proxy posture (decided): grade-1 primary' (flint-lean-plan.md §2.2) and 'Presigned grade-2 (un-deferred only by a measured 0c proxy bottleneck)' (§8). As decided and built, every publish byte transits a flint-deployed proxy ('agents contact it only', §1) plus a separate gateway hop, and no document specifies transit encryption for either in-cluster hop. krb5p's 4.5 is documented per-RPC GSS privacy; FUSE's 4.5 is a single hop to the S3 endpoint where TLS is the endpoint's own guarantee (presigned URLs are https). Lean's extra unspecified hops put it half a step below: 4.0.

The number survives, though the cited quote is superseded: the plan's corrected failure model is broader than 'publishes pause' — 'gateway/proxy down ⇒ publishes pause AND checkouts/restarts wedge AND sync is unavailable AND HITL UI writes fail' (flint-lean-plan.md §2.2/§7). But the damage a credential-less peer can do remains availability-only and control-plane-only: the gateway holds 'no PVC, no epoch of its own, no state — everything durable is in the bucket' (flint-lean-architecture.html), so there is no B6-class state minting, and 'running pods keep serving local files throughout' (§7). The 0.5 dock under FUSE (no flint-run door at all, AWS absorbs the flood) already prices the two flint-run doors, the unmeasured Phase 0c burst rig, and the unbuilt checkout-admission token. 4 is calibrated against sys/krb5p at 2.5 (hub-down hangs every mount) and FUSE at 4.5.

Score survives, but on corrected grounds: the proposer's B12 discriminator is non-differential — FUSE's design closes the same class ('share identity, If-None-Match:* at birth — kills prefix-reuse adoption', flint-fuse-architecture.html p.2). What actually sustains 4 over FUSE's 3.5 is the single-principal restoration: pods hold no store credentials at all, so cross-project reach requires compromising the proxy itself, whereas FUSE's own doc concedes 'The bucket no longer trusts one principal' with every pod holding prefix-scoped bucket credentials whose correctness rests on per-workspace IAM authoring (the doc flags PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration as 'a bucket-wide delete lever'). The counterweight — FUSE refuses cross-workspace at 'IAM scope ends at ws-a/' granularity while lean is 'gateway-validated + CAS-cooperative... versioning recovers' within a project (§3) — is real but sits inside the project boundary, and the axis is defined at tenant/project granularity, where lean's boundary is data-plane native and enforced. The within-project residual correctly keeps it off 4.5.

Survives refutation. Doc claims hold: 'pods hold ZERO bucket write credentials', sidecar 'ordinary process — UNPRIVILEGED, no /dev/fuse... no PSA conflict', 'revocation in seconds — kill the token' (flint-lean-architecture.html). The strongest counter — as built, the compromised pod's proxy token writes the whole project prefix directly, control cells included, since barriers bypass the gateway ('they currently CAS the cells directly through the proxy', plan status header) — is already carved into the rationale, is versioning-recoverable ('bucket versioning makes clobbers recoverable', §3), stays project-bounded, and per the scoring rules the enforced-arbitration path is scored as designed where unbuilt. The relative gaps hold: FUSE 1.5 (real cloud credentials in every pod, usable from anywhere until IAM revocation propagates, pod is epoch holder), krb5p 3.5 (Kerberos tickets remain valid until expiry after KDC revocation vs lean's seconds-scale token kill). 4.5 with 5 withheld for the project-wide token is right.

All cited quotes verified: 'no token ⇒ routes are not mounted (404, not 401)' (file-api-fleet-auth.md line 34), the chart 'refuses to render... a helm error, not a running open proxy' (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md ~line 82), the conformance gate's must-FAIL arms 'refusing barriers while drifted' (flint-lean-plan.md §2.2), 'failurePolicy: Fail still applies' (flint-lean-architecture.html), foreign claim ⇒ 'refusing status condition, never on-the-fly adoption' and checkout refusing over-budget (§2.4, §1). The transferred hub-gateway evidence is legitimate since the lean gateway's recommended home is extending flint-hub-gateway (§9.1). The 0.5 edge over FUSE (also 'failurePolicy: Fail' + an unforgeable IAM second layer, all designed-only) is doc-grounded in lean's smaller misconfigurable surface — 'everything the FUSE recipe needs for privilege, brokers and /dev/fuse is simply not needed' — plus anti-vacuity arms proven to fail against naive implementations. Phase 4 being unbuilt is honestly stated and applies equally to FUSE's webhook.

axes.name: Failure shape
axes.definition: How component failures present to running workloads: blast radius, hang vs error vs bounded loss, and the recovery ceremony they demand.

axes.name: Upgrades & restart recovery
axes.definition: Cost and risk of rolling new versions and recovering from process/container restarts under live workloads.

axes.name: Fleet-scale standing footprint
axes.definition: Standing objects, control-plane load, and recurring coordination cost when the share count reaches thousands.

axes.name: Fleet observability
axes.definition: Ability to answer 'is it healthy, is it clean, what is the RPO' per share from an operable fleet-wide surface.

axes.name: Consumer footprint
axes.definition: What must be installed, privileged, or configured on client nodes and pods for the data path to keep working day to day.

axes.name: Idle lifecycle & wake
axes.definition: Cost of a parked share and the safety and latency of winding down and waking back up.

cells.rationale: The failure matrix's hub-NODE-crash row is the worst shape on any page: 'every client hard-hangs in D-state; Recreate + RWO + ~6 min force-detach; F29's manual arm' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p4), and the fleets guide confirms hard-mount clients enter uninterruptible sleep SIGKILL cannot touch, wedging the container runtime itself (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md). Rare but share-wide and hang-shaped; only the benign pod-crash case (13s, clients park and resume) keeps it off the floor.

Same hub concentration, so the identical D-state/force-detach class applies unchanged; the GSS layer (dormant in-tree, scored as designed) changes nothing about the hang shape while adding KDC/keytab/rpc.gssd infrastructure as further mount-path dependencies (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117).

As designed: 'a dead mount is ENOTCONN — an error, never a D-state hang', and failure distributes into 'frequent, per-pod, LOSS-shaped events' — durability becomes an operational statistic, with node crash losing the unflushed set plus a 60-110s subtree write-lockout (flint-fuse-architecture.html p4). Errors beat hangs, but the loss class is permanent and hub mode does not have it.
