'Gateway down => publishes pause and the RPO grows while pods keep serving local files — far softer than hub-down; reads never depended on it' — 'the softest failure shape any component on these pages has' (flint-lean-architecture.html). Held to 3.5 by the corrected §7: a gateway/proxy outage also wedges checkouts, restarts, sync, and HITL writes fleet-wide (flint-lean-plan.md §7); built through Phase 3 with the outage drill still open.

Hub restarts are measured-benign — 'restart + epoch re-claim ≈ 13s; clients park and resume — nothing durable at risk (PVC)' (flint-fuse-architecture.html matrix), MDS roll ~40s with max client stall 1s (pnfs-operator-runbook.md). Docked for single-replica Recreate (a config change rolls the pod) and G15's rollback trap: any SCHEMA_VERSION bump makes rollback a crash-loop, per the 1.26/1.27 must-skip precedent (docs/plans/nfs-server-hardening-plan.md G15).

Everything the sys hub carries, plus per-node keytabs and rpc.gssd become part of every client-node lifecycle event (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117). The implementation is dormant — 'wiring it up... is the documented strong-auth path' — so no roll of this stack has ever been exercised; scored as designed.

As designed: 'upgrade = pod churn: injection is create-time only... a flint-fuse CVE reaches the fleet by pod churn, so stale-sidecar reporting is part of the operator's job' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p2), and restart is a fragile contract — 'the reflex — restart the pod — destroys exactly the dirty set a container restart would have saved', plus the 80-110s lease tax on unclean death (p4).

Container restart over a live tree is a first-class state in the shipped restart matrix — 'never re-materialize: reload the persisted baseline, rescan to rebuild dirt, self-recognize the lease via the persisted incarnation id' (flint-lean-plan.md §2.1, battery-tested through Phase 2/3) — and §7 states 'no recovery-order contract, no daemon in the data path'. Sidecar upgrades still ride create-time injection, but an unprivileged ordinary process makes the stakes far lower than FUSE's.

The fleet math is explicit: 'hub: 3000 Services (73% of a /20 CIDR) · 3000 PVCs · the ladder' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p2), and the fleet-scale plan records that cold start at 3000 CRs was a deterministic OOMKill (B3) with kube-proxy at 3000 Services still an extrapolation (docs/plans/flint-lite-fleet-scale-plan.md). The rate-term blockers are fixed, but the per-share standing-object ladder is by design.

Inherits the hub's entire 3000-object ladder and adds fleet-wide security infrastructure on top: a KDC plus keytab distribution to every client node (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117) — standing state the sys posture does not carry, on every node in every consumer cluster.

As designed, 'mode: direct — NOTHING standing... one webhook, one bucket', but the same page prices the coordination residue: 'epoch heartbeats: 3000 cells at 10s defaults ≈ $3.9k/mo' pending lease-only-while-dirty, and a 1000-pod reclaim wave 'must not LIST an unpartitioned bucket into a 503 storm' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p2/p3).

'Idle = S3 only, structurally. Lease cells exist only while a writer runs' (flint-lean-plan.md §6): nothing standing per share, one per-cluster stateless gateway. Costs are per-activity rather than per-share — publish amplification (a hot 2 GiB file ≈ 2.9 TiB/day at 60s cadence) is 'bounded by policy, not physics' via the per-file cooldown, and proxy replica sizing has a formula but Phase 0c is unmeasured.

The best-instrumented surface of the four: /status 'tells importing from wedged', exposes recovery point, epoch holder, and the NFS client list (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md), hibernate is 'verify-then-delete, never assume' on the rpoClean witness, and 'the fleet is one command' — kubectl get flintshares -A with phase/address/conditions (flint-lite-architecture.html p2/p4). Docked for documented silent traps: a wrong PV address hangs with 'no event at all' on kind.

Same /status + CRD surface, but the GSS path itself has no operational instrumentation — it is dormant, validated only 'via pynfs --security=krb5' (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117) — so keytab/context/ticket failures arrive as a new uninstrumented diagnosis class on a wire where every RPC is GSS-wrapped.

The design deletes the fleet's best witness and replaces it with the bucket: 'FUSE mode has no equivalent witness [to rpoClean], so the bucket (manifest seq and age per workspace...) becomes the only global status surface', with alerting moved there and per-pod metrics merely owed from webhook injection (flint-fuse-architecture.html p4); the loss-event rate 'is a property of the fleet and must be measured there'.

Phase 3 names concrete deliverables — 'per-pod RPO gauge (seconds-since-last-barrier + unpublished bytes), publish-failure and checkout-wedged alerts, conflict-report surfacing' — and sync emits a machine-readable conflict report (flint-lean-plan.md §5/§2.1). Gateway verbs are shipped but the gauges/alerts are not confirmed shipped, and there is no hub-style live client list; the gateway is at least a central vantage the FUSE design lacks.

'Nothing from flint installed' — the data path is the node kernel's NFS client and 'consumers never get bucket credentials' (flint-lite-architecture.html p1/p3). The residue is config traps, not software: without nconnect>=2 the kernel 'silently refuses every additional trunk — no error, on either side, ever', and client names must be fleet-unique.

'Wiring it up (KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd, sec=krb5p mount opts)' (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117): every client node gains a keytab, a userspace daemon, and a Kerberos realm dependency — the heaviest ongoing consumer requirement of the four series, for a stack that is dormant in-tree today.

As designed, the injected sidecar is 'privileged · Bidirectional · /dev/fuse' in every matched pod, 'PSA baseline / restricted refuse privileged sidecars' — forcing a node-broker endgame — and there is a kernel floor of 'plain fuse3' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p1/p2). Nothing to install per node, but a heavy, privilege-laden per-pod contract.

The sidecar is an 'ordinary process — UNPRIVILEGED — no /dev/fuse · no mount propagation... no PSA conflict' and 'the kernel floor drops to nothing' (flint-lean-architecture.html); pods hold zero bucket credentials. Held under sys because native sidecar containers are MANDATORY (K8s >= 1.29) and every pod still takes webhook injection plus an emptyDir budget (flint-lean-plan.md §2.4).

The two-rung ladder gives disk-only then S3-only cost with a verified drain (wake ~41s / ~79s from Hibernated, flint-lite-architecture.html p4), but suspendWithSessions 'defaults to suspending anyway; the protective value is opt-in', and suspending under a live hard mount is 'not data loss; an indefinite hang' that no NFS client can undo (flint-lite-for-agent-fleets.md).

The ladder and its hazards are unchanged — the GSS layer rides the same :2049 data path and the runbook's Kerberos section (pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~109-117) states no interaction with park/wake, so the score matches sys; scored as designed on the dormant implementation.

As designed, 'idle = Hibernated, structurally' — 'the idle LADDER becomes vacuous, and with it the B6-class inversions and the rpoClean/PVC-delete coupling' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p2). The stated price: 'every pod start is a Hibernated-class cold start', plus heartbeat economics until lease-only-while-dirty and version reaping land.

'Idle = S3 only, structurally. Lease cells exist only while a writer runs' (flint-lean-plan.md §6): no ladder, no suspend hazard, no keepalive protocol to get wrong. Cold start is a full-workspace checkout through the proxy whose rate is a Phase 0b acceptance number still unmeasured — the one open risk keeping it off 4.

proposal.note: Day-2 operations is where the hub's concentration costs the most: both NFS variants inherit hang-shaped, share-wide failures (D-state clients, ~6 min force-detach, F29's manual arm) and a 3000-Service standing ladder, and krb5p subtracts further on every axis it touches by adding KDC/keytab/rpc.gssd to each client node. The direct modes invert the picture — nothing standing, idle equals S3 structurally — and Lean beats FUSE nearly everywhere by shedding privilege, the restart-in-place choreography, and the loss-statistics failure class. The exception is observability: the hub's rpoClean witness and /status remain the fleet's best-instrumented surface, while FUSE's bucket-only status is the weakest cell on the chart. Lean's caveat is a new fleet-wide wedge point: a gateway/proxy outage pauses publishes but also wedges checkouts, restarts, sync, and HITL writes.

Verified: 'Consumer cluster — nothing from flint installed', 'Consumers never get bucket credentials — the bucket trusts one principal: the hub' (lite-arch p1), 'Consumers install nothing from flint either way: the data path is the node kernel's NFS client' (p3). The sys baseline is real — flint-lite-fleet-scale-plan.md line 211: '3000 CRs plus ~15,000 child objects' — and krb5p strictly adds a KDC plus keytab distribution to every client node ('KDC, per-node keytabs, rpc.gssd', pnfs-operator-runbook.md ~111), standing security state sys does not carry. Attempted refutation against FUSE=1.5 fails: FUSE's burden (privileged /dev/fuse sidecar, Bidirectional, webhook injection — flint-fuse-architecture.html pages 2/5) is in-cluster and webhook-automated with a documented 'unprivileged endgame', while the same doc calls the hub 'the zero-consumer-requirements path', anchoring sys=4; krb5p uniquely adds off-cluster standing infrastructure per node.

A ticket-expiry-at-wake penalty would be undocumented speculation, so 2.5 = sys survives.

Score 3 survives refutation in both directions. Above sys/krb5p 1.5 is doc-forced: 'a dead mount is ENOTCONN — an error, never a D-state hang' and 'one pod's staleness is one pod's problem' vs the hub's 'every client hard-hangs in D-state; Recreate + RWO + ~6 min force-detach; F29's manual arm' (flint-fuse-architecture.html p4; flint-consistency-comparison.html 'direct wins latency and failure shape'). As designed, unbuilt (git 63e0e20: FUSE track deprioritized).

Score 2 survives. I tested whether the clean-drain path (preStop ~17s fast path) lifts FUSE to sys's 2.5: it does not, because upgrades structurally require churning every workload pod ('upgrade = pod churn: injection is create-time only... a flint-fuse CVE reaches the fleet by pod churn', p2) where a hub roll parks clients ~13s with 'nothing durable at risk (PVC)'. Restart recovery is a trained ceremony with the worst trap in any column: 'the reflex — restart the pod — destroys exactly the dirty set a container restart would have saved', 'open fds stay severed — apps reopen', and 'a fresh emptyDir defeats self-recognition... 60s configured, 80–110s measured' (p4). The gap to Lean 3.5 is real: lean restart is 'lease self-recognized, dirt rebuilt by rescan' with the app untouched (flint-lean-plan.md §7) and a stateless N-replica gateway.

I tested pushing above Lean's 3.5 on 'mode: direct — NOTHING standing... zero pods, zero Services, zero PVCs' vs hub's '3000 Services (73% of a /20 CIDR) · 3000 PVCs · the ladder' (p2) — but the FUSE doc prices its own coordination residue: 'epoch heartbeats: 3000 cells at 10s defaults ≈ $3.9k/mo — lease only while dirty; land tag-filtered version reaping first' (mitigations unbuilt), 'bucket Versioning is a HARD requirement in this mode', the 1000-pod reclaim wave 503-storm discipline (p3), and p5 concedes per-POD sidecars 'multiply' cache/disk/lease — 'the largest single lever on every duplication term'. Well above sys 1.5/krb5p 1 regardless.

Score 1.5 survives an attempted push to 2. The relocated surface is real as designed — 'the bucket (manifest seq and age per workspace, CAS-versioned and readable by a plain S3 client) becomes the only global status surface' plus operator report step 5 'manifest age per workspace replaces the hub's /status' (p2/p4) — but the axis asks 'is it clean, what is the RPO', and FUSE structurally cannot answer the first: 'FUSE mode has no equivalent witness' to rpoClean, dirty state lives in per-pod emptyDir, manifest age cannot distinguish idle-clean from stuck-dirty, and the loss rate 'is a property of the fleet and must be measured there' — a statistic, not a per-share observation. Per-pod metrics are merely owed from injection. Lean at 3 has what FUSE lacks: every publish transits a gateway grant with 'per-share metering' restored. The floor position vs all three others is doc-grounded; the 0.5 upward push has no decisive evidence.

Score 1.5 survives an attempted drop to 1 (tie with krb5p) and any upward push. The per-pod contract is privilege-laden: 'privileged · Bidirectional · /dev/fuse' in every matched pod, native sidecar needs 'GA K8s 1.33', 'every pod holds bucket credentials — prefix-scoped IAM', and 'PSA baseline / restricted refuse privileged sidecars' — the escape is a whole extra component, 'an unprivileged injected sidecar + a stateless node broker... named the production endgame for PSA-restricted fleets' (p1/p2). That caps it far below Lean 3.5 ('no /dev/fuse · no mount propagation · no privileged · no PSA conflict', pods hold 'ZERO bucket write credentials'). But it stays a notch above krb5p 1: the app side is clean ('unchanged image · no bucket credentials', 'the consumer kernel plays no part — no NFS client, no PVC, no Service', kernel floor 'plain fuse3') versus provisioning per-client keytabs/KDC for dormant in-tree machinery (pnfs-operator-runbook.md is its only mention).

findings.detail: Recurring dollar cost at fleet scale is load-bearing in the docs but has no axis in any chart. The FUSE doc prices its own design ('epoch heartbeats: 3000 cells at 10s defaults ≈ $3.9k/mo — lease only while dirty', flint-fuse-architecture.html:345); the lean plan has a whole section titled '6. Economics (amplification stated, not hidden)' with 'a 2 GiB hot file re-uploads whole per barrier (~2.9 TiB/day at 60 s)' (flint-lean-plan.md:370-377); the hub gateway doc calls hibernate wake 'a full DR import from the bucket each: real billed egress' (flint-hub-gateway.md:308). Right now cost leaks inconsistently into day2 'Fleet-scale standing footprint': FUSE's 3 is explicitly docked for the $3.9k/mo term, but lean's 3.5 forgives its 2.9 TiB/day amplification as 'bounded by policy, not physics', and the hub's billed-egress wake cost is docked nowhere. Series conclusions would change: lean's publish amplification and FUSE's heartbeat/versioning-storage taxes are their docs' own headline liabilities.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'recurring cost at fleet scale' axis (S3 request+egress+storage per share-month, standing compute) to the day2 chart or a fifth mini-chart, and strip the dollar terms out of 'Fleet-scale standing footprint' so that axis scores only standing objects/control-plane load.

findings.detail: Workload/capacity envelope — which workloads a series can even admit — is the docs' own routing decision, and no chart expresses it. flint-fuse-architecture.html p5 is literally a routing table: 'route to the hub' for 'large-artifact writers (dirty > ~10 GiB)' (line 750) and the p4 figcaption calls 'shared-RWX trees, multi-pod sqlite/git, large-artifact writers' strictly worse on FUSE; lean's dirtySetCapGiB is arithmetically tied to spot grace (flint-lean-plan.md:179-186) and checkout refuses over-budget workspaces; only the hub (PVC + tier) hosts working sets larger than node-local disk. Worse, several performance scores are already conditioned on staying inside the envelope — the FUSE streaming-write 4 was defended by 'p5 explicitly routes large-artifact writers (dirty > ~10 GiB) to the hub' — so the radar shows FUSE/Lean beating the hub 4-5 vs 3 on write throughput while hiding that the workloads where that matters most are inadmissible on FUSE/Lean. A reader routing a 50 GiB-working-set tenant off this chart picks the wrong front end.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'workload envelope' axis (max working set / max dirty set / shared-tree admissibility) to performance or day2, scoring hub ~5, lean/FUSE ~2, and annotate the streaming-write cells as 'within envelope'.

findings.detail: Perf 'Cold start' and day2 'Idle lifecycle & wake' price substantially the same facts and produce inverted orderings: perf has sys 4 > krb5p 3.5 = FUSE 3.5 > Lean 3; day2 has Lean 3.5 > FUSE 3 > sys 2.5. The perf axis definition includes 'first access after idle/eviction', and on that leg the hub is the documented WORST series: IdleSuspended wake 11s floor with bad paths >25s, and 'A Hibernated share is a full DR import from the bucket and will time out here by design' (flint-hub-gateway.md:288-289), hydrate measured 72.5 s/GiB (runbs) / 131 s for 1 GiB (fleets guide:907) — versus lean's measured 3.3 s/GiB checkout (flint-lean-0b-measurements.md:32), ~20-40x faster per GiB even granting FLOOR caveats. The sys=4 verdict anchors on the warm-hub best case ('a new pod pays only a mount') while lean's 3 anchors on its pay-everything-upfront worst case — same axis, different assumptions per series. Additionally FUSE's cold-start dock cites the 60-110s write lockout while lean's cell never mentions the analogous checkout-gate wedge risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the axis cleanly: perf 'Cold start' = new pod against a live/warm share (sys 4-4.5, FUSE ~3.5, Lean ~2.5-3 is then coherent); move ALL after-idle/hibernated wake into day2 'Idle & wake' (where Lean > FUSE > sys already matches the docs), and state the anchor in each axis definition.

findings.detail: The consistency chart has three series while the other three charts have four, and the series key is inconsistent: consistency cells use 'NFS' where the other charts use 'sys' and 'krb5p'. krb5p has no consistency polygon in the data at all — the claim that it inherits NFS's scores exists only as a sentence inside one verdict rationale ('krb5p wraps the RPCs without changing their meaning, so it inherits the 5'). Rendered as a 4-series radar set, krb5p silently vanishes from chart 1, or a renderer keyed on series names ('sys' vs 'NFS') drops/mislabels the hub series in chart 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add explicit krb5p rows to the consistency cells (duplicating NFS values) or rename 'NFS' to 'sys' and add a stated legend note 'krb5p ≡ sys on consistency'; unify series identifiers across all four dims.

findings.detail: The four series sit at wildly different maturity (hub shipped+drilled; krb5p dormant, never wired, pynfs-only; FUSE designed-only and deprioritized per commit 63e0e20; lean built through Phase 3 with drills open), the docs treat provenness as load-bearing (FUSE: '4 gates + 4 preconditions before ANY code'; lean 0b gate 'closes only when re-measured PROXY-SHAPED'), yet no chart represents maturity — so build-state discounts leak into substantive axes ad hoc. Inconsistent applications in the recorded verdicts: FUSE client-auth 3.5 is held down by a 'designed-not-built dock' and FUSE tenancy by 'not yet load-bearing as coded'; krb5p wire 4.5 is discounted for being 'dormant homegrown'; but lean pod-compromise 4.5 invokes the opposite rule ('per the scoring rules the enforced-arbitration path is scored as designed where unbuilt'), and FUSE DoS/wire 4.5 carry no dormancy dock at all. The same meta-fact (unbuiltness) is a shave in some cells and inadmissible in others, biasing cross-series gaps unpredictably.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one rule (score as-designed everywhere), re-audit every cell that cited build state as a score input, and surface maturity separately — a per-series badge (shipped / built-partial / designed / dormant) on every chart, or a dedicated maturity axis on day2.

findings.detail: The single measured fact '60s configured, 80-110s measured lease lockout after unclean death' is priced against FUSE in four cells across three charts — consistency Multi-writer arbitration (1.5), perf Cold start (3.5 dock), day2 Upgrades (2), day2 Failure shape (3 rationale) — while the verdicts themselves state lean 'carries the identical lockout' (lean arbitration verdict: 'does not drag it below 2.5 because FUSE carries the identical lockout') yet lean is docked for it in at most one cell (day2 Upgrades mention; lean's perf Cold start and Failure shape never mention it). One fact repeatedly deflating one series' silhouette while being waived for the series that shares it is a systematic asymmetry, not four independent observations.
findings.suggested_fix: Home the lockout in exactly one axis per chart-family (day2 Upgrades & restart recovery is the natural owner), and wherever it is kept, apply it symmetrically to FUSE and Lean or explicitly state why lean's exposure differs (e.g., checkout-fresh pods vs restart-in-place).

findings.detail: Three instances of one underlying fact lowering two axes of the same chart. (a) day2/sys: the idle-suspend-under-live-mount hang ('an NFS client cannot write a Kubernetes annotation... Not data loss; an indefinite hang', fleets guide:973-979) is cited as the 'second hang class' holding Failure shape at 1.5 AND is the core dock on Idle & wake 2.5 — but idle suspend is a lifecycle action, not a component failure, so it is out-of-definition in Failure shape and double-priced. (b) security/krb5p: the server accepting AUTH_UNIX alongside GSS with no flavor-enforcement policy (server_v4.rs) is the stated reason for BOTH the auth-strength shave 4.5→4 ('the floor stays AUTH_SYS') and the misconfig cap at 2 ('the server side fails open') — fail-open-on-omission is precisely the misconfig axis's subject, so it should be priced once.
